# Pila

Pila is a free browser tool that checks whether your batteries are ready for the EU digital battery passport under the Batteries Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1542), mandatory from 18 February 2027. It runs entirely in the browser (no data leaves the device).

## Key facts (verified 14 August 2026)

- Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 entered into force on 17 February 2024 and applies to all batteries placed on the EU market: portable, LMT (light means of transport), SLI, EV and industrial batteries.
- From 18 February 2027 (Art. 77), every EV battery, LMT battery above 2 kWh and industrial battery above 2 kWh placed on the EU market or put into service must have a battery passport linked by QR code — no passport, no placement.
- The passport record includes manufacturer identity, model, capacity, chemistry and materials, carbon footprint, performance and durability, and state-of-health history.
- Carbon footprint declaration for EV batteries applies since 18 February 2025; performance class labelling since 18 February 2026.
- From 18 August 2028, passports must document recycled content (cobalt, lithium, nickel, lead).
- Enforcement: market surveillance can block, restrict or withdraw non-compliant batteries; penalties are set by each Member State.

## Pricing

- Free: passport gap check + checklist + market-access exposure.
- Pro (8 USD one-time, crypto): printable passport stamp PDF, passport data-set template, Art. 77 readiness checklist, permanent unlock.

## Not advice

Pila is an educational tool based on Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. It is not legal or technical advice. Editorial responsibility: attenciona (Holding), Spain.
